brief: The action of the Virasoro algebra in quantum spin chains. I. The non-rational case — We investigate the action of discretized Virasoro generators, built out of generators of the lattice
extended:
**The action of the Virasoro algebra in quantum spin chains. I. The non-rational case**

*Linnea Grans-Samuelsson 1, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen 1,2,3,4, and Hubert Saleur 1,5*

61 pp, 52 sections.

**Abstract.** We investigate the action of discretized Virasoro generators, built out of generators of the lattice Temperley-Lieb algebra (“Koo-Saleur generators” [1]), in the critical XXZ quantum spin chain. We ex- plore the structure of the continuum-limit Virasoro modules at generic central charge for the XXZ vertex model, paralleling [2] for the loop model. We ﬁnd again indecomposable modules, but this time not loga- rithmic ones. The limit of the Temperley-Lieb modules Wj,1 for j ⁄= 0 contains pairs of “conjugate states” with conformal weights ( hr,s, hr,−s) and ( hr,−s, hr,s) that give rise to dual structures: Verma or co-Verma modules. The limit of W0,q±2 contains diagonal ﬁelds (hr,1, hr,1) and gives rise to either only Verma or only co-Verma modules, depending on the sign of the exponent in q±2.

**Outline.** Front matter; 1 Introduction; 2 Discrete Virasoro algebra and the Koo-Saleur; 2.1 The Temperley-Lieb algebra in the periodic; 2.1.1 The algebra TaN(m); 2.1.2 Standard modules; 2.2 Physical systems and the Temperley-Lieb Ha; 2.3 Indecomposability; 2.4 Discrete Virasoro algebra; 3 Some features of the continuum limit; 3.1 Modules in the continuum; 3.2 Bosonization and expected results; 3.3 The choices of metric; 3.4 Feigin-Fuchs modules and conjugate states; 4 Bethe Ansatz picture; 4.1 Bethe-ansatz and the identification of sca; 4.1.1 Overlaps and mixing; 4.2 Conjugate states and Bethe roots
